text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak will announce within hours the start of work on the new delta in southern Egypt. Prime Minister Ganzouri tells reporters that the president will deliver an international message affirming the government's intent to give incentives and higher wages to workers in the project.
- President's wife inaugurates the village housing flood victims in Luxor.
- Panel in London says southern delta project has opened broader horizons for reclaiming the desert.
- Official spokesman of Egypt's interior ministry denies from Tunis that Moslem militants attacked the Montazah palace in Alexandria.
- Mubarak to visit Washington in March and U.S. vice president Al Gore to visit Egypt next month.
- The secret meeting between Arafat and Netanyahu has failed. Israel denies that it has given up its demands for hot pursuit in the Palestinian territories.
- Al-Azhar university opinion poll shows that Mubarak is the bastion of peace and Islam and that Al-Akhbar is the best newspaper.
- Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq el-Mahdi says that Egypt's acheivements are the pride of the Arab world.
- Head of investment authority says that investment incentives in Egypt are better than any other country.
- Study shows that pumping station at the Sheikh Zayed canal needs 700 megawatts, or 20 percent of the output of the Aswan High Dam, to work.
- Arafat and Netanyahu meet in secret for six hours in Gaza. Egyptian Foreign Minister Moussa says he has received news of progress in the Hebron talks.
- Mubarak calls Syrian president Assad to discuss regional issues.
